lines.trans: Give a hand signal on the floor asking Cindy to keep her acceptance speech super brief after the winner announcement!
Cindy's speeches are always just "thank you" and done—she would not cry even if she won first place a hundred times.
Thank you! Today's trophy carries so many meanings for me—I want to share my heart with the people I am grateful to.
Wait, what is gotten into her?! Did nobody tell Cindy we are out of broadcast time?!
First, thank you to my older sisters in Pinky4, and I am sorry—I never once said it aloud, yet I really loved you all.
To my parents watching from afar, I want to tell you how much I miss you and love you.
At this rate she is about to thank her elementary-school teacher! Cut the mic or cue the encore music—wait, hold on!
Though I made so many mistakes, thank you to Tak Ye-jin for grumbling up front while caring for me behind the scenes—and Producer Ra Joon-mo of 2 Days & 1 Night!
Whoa whoa, why is she thanking 2 Days & 1 Night on my show?! Cut it, cut it!
And finally, to the person who became my umbrella when I stood alone in the pouring rain—thank you from the bottom of my heart.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 정권 바뀌면 바꿀 게 한두 가지가 아니에요.
examples.trans: When leadership changes, there is way more than one or two things you have to change.
Here the word for 'kinds, items' is key.

meanings.note: Used as casual present (간단해.).

examples.text: 그래 집주인이니까 네가 결정해. 변 대표한테 전화해서 데리러 오라고 그러면 그게 제일 간단해.
examples.trans: Fine, you are the homeowner, so you decide—calling CEO Byun to come pick her up is the simplest option.
It is really is simple compared to what I expected.
Thank you for helping.
Yes, that's right.

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?

meanings.note: Native Korean expression of thanks; 고마워요 is warm and polite.

examples.trans: Thank you so much for helping me.
Thank you always.

meanings.note: Softens a statement or downplays a motive.

examples.trans: I just asked out of curiosity.
I'll just stay home today.
I bought bread. And I bought milk too.
Let's eat and then depart.

meanings.note: Used as noun + casual copula (기세야!).

examples.text: 지금 초등학교 선생님한테까지 고맙다고 할 기세야! 야 끊어, 음악을 때리든가!
examples.trans: At this rate she is about to thank her elementary-school teacher! Cut the mic or cue the encore music—wait, hold on!
This point about momentum she is on is really important.
I'll hang up the phone.
I quit smoking.

meanings.note: Used colloquially for positive or negative emphasis.
Original sense of exceeding a limit.

examples.trans: The weather is so nice today.
Don't worry too much.

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.

meanings.note: Usually followed by -e to express gratitude for someone's help.

examples.trans: Thanks to you, I'm doing well.
It is all thanks to the teacher.

meanings.note: Used as honorific past adnominal (되어주셨던…).

examples.text: 마지막으로 제가 빗속에 혼자 서 있을 때 우산이 되어주셨던… 덕분에 감사하다고 말씀드리고 싶어요.
examples.trans: And finally, to the person who became my umbrella when I stood alone in the pouring rain—thank you from the bottom of my heart.
Let us do that (became for me…) right away.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 그래서 요 며칠 내 뒤를 졸졸 따라다니면서 선배를 떠봐?
examples.trans: So that is why you trailed behind me like a puppy these past few days sounding out your senior?
Here the word for 'behind me' is key.

meanings.note: Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

examples.trans: Call me when you have time.
I lived in this neighborhood when I was young.

meanings.note: Used as present adnominal (때리는).

examples.text: 야 승찬아, 너도 그날 봤잖아, 변 대표가 그 매니저 뺨 때리는 거.
examples.trans: Hey Seung-chan, you saw it that day too—CEO Byun slapping that manager across the face.
Let us do that (slapping) right away.

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.

examples.trans: See you again!
It is raining again.
Did you hear about this to my liking?
I was busy today because of to my liking.

meanings.note: Can modify a following noun directly (마지막 촬영지) or take 으로 (마지막으로, 'finally').

examples.trans: Today is the last day.
Please ask the final question.

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.

meanings.en: a lot, much, in large quantity
meanings.note: Adverbial form of 많다 (to be many/much)

examples.trans: I did a lot of work today.
Please eat plenty and enjoy.

meanings.note: Combines with 하다 in 말하다 (to speak, to say).

examples.trans: I don't know what you mean.
You speak Korean well.
I want to humbly tell him right now.
How about trying to humbly tell him together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Used as adverb (멀리서).

examples.text: 멀리서 지켜보고 계실 부모님, 보고 싶고 또 사랑한다고 전하고 싶고요.
examples.trans: To my parents watching from afar, I want to tell you how much I miss you and love you.
I thought it over again (from afar).

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.text: 어제는 너무 피곤해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.trans: I was so tired yesterday that I couldn't sleep.
Because it rained, we couldn't go on the picnic.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?
Is something the matter?

meanings.en: to be sorry; to feel apologetic
meanings.note: Descriptive adjective; used with peers or younger people (whereas 죄송하다 is honorific/humble).

examples.trans: I'm really sorry I'm late.

examples.text: 미안하지만 다시 한 번 말씀해 주세요.
examples.trans: I'm sorry, but please say that one more time.

meanings.note: Used as noun (발표).

examples.text: 신디 1위 발표 후에 소감만 아주 간단하게 해달라고 수신호 좀 해주세요!
examples.trans: Give a hand signal on the floor asking Cindy to keep her acceptance speech super brief after the winner announcement!
This point about announcement is really important.

meanings.note: Follows native Korean numbers (한 번, 두 번, 세 번) to count how many times.

examples.trans: I watched this movie three times.
Please explain it just one more time.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 내가 혼자서 자유로운 싱글의 삶을 누려보려고 부모님한테 어렵게 얻어낸 집인데,
examples.trans: I worked so hard to talk my parents into getting this place so I could enjoy a free single life alone…
Here the word for 'from my parents' is key.

meanings.note: Honorific noun and counter for people, used instead of 사람.

examples.trans: That person over there is our teacher.
How many people are in your party?

meanings.note: Used as compound noun + locative (빗속에).

examples.text: 마지막으로 제가 빗속에 혼자 서 있을 때 우산이 되어주셨던… 덕분에 감사하다고 말씀드리고 싶어요.
examples.trans: And finally, to the person who became my umbrella when I stood alone in the pouring rain—thank you from the bottom of my heart.

examples.trans: Give a hand signal on the floor asking Cindy to keep her acceptance speech super brief after the winner announcement!
This point about a hand signal is really important.

meanings.note: Available time or duration.
Used with native Korean numbers to count hours (한 시간 = one hour).

examples.trans: Do you have time?
It takes two hours.

meanings.note: Used as noun + causal -로 (실수로).

examples.text: 아, 마지막에 이거 넣으라고, 한편 신디는 얼마 전 특집쇼 녹화 중 담당 여자 피디인 티모 피디의 실수로 부상을 입어 입원을 한 바 있다.
examples.trans: Oh, and put this at the end: Meanwhile, Cindy was recently hospitalized after being injured during a special taping due to a mistake by female producer T.
This point about due to a mistake is really important.

meanings.note: Auxiliary adjective attached to a verb stem with -고 (-고 싶다).

examples.trans: I want to go to Korea.
I want to drink a cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Oh, I see!

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 변 대표랑 준모랑 서로 쌍소리 오가고 촬영장 아주 개판 됐대요.
examples.trans: They say CEO Byun and Joon-mo traded harsh words and the set turned into a total mess.
Here the word for 'completely' is key.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

meanings.note: noun

examples.trans: Go forward.
Do well in the future.

meanings.note: Casual exclamation used to call someone younger or a close friend.

examples.trans: Hey, come quickly!
Hey, where are you going?
Did you hear about this older sister, idol?
I was busy today because of older sister, idol.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.
Did you hear about this several?
I was busy today because of several.

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.
What day of the week is it today?

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean term.

examples.trans: Since it's raining, please use an umbrella.
I lost my umbrella.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: ㄹ drops before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g. 우세요, 웁니다).

examples.trans: I cried because the movie was sad.
The baby is crying loudly.

meanings.note: describes how things typically work
refers to an initial state or plan

examples.trans: Traffic is usually heavy on Mondays.
This place was originally a park.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 음악이라도 들으시면 잠이 잘 오실 거예요.
examples.trans: If you listen to at least some music, you should fall asleep more easily.
Here the word for 'even just music' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 좀 더 자숙하는 의미로 한복 입고 가면 어떨까?
examples.trans: To show deeper self-reflection, how about wearing traditional Korean attire?
Here the word for 'as a gesture of' is key.

meanings.note: demonstrative determiner placed before a noun

examples.text: 이 바닥은 자기 밥그릇은 자기가 챙겨야 돼.
examples.trans: In this industry, you have to look after your own rice bowl.
This book is interesting.

meanings.en: first of all, for starters, for the time being
meanings.note: marks an immediate first step before dealing with anything else

examples.trans: Let's sit down and talk first.
Let's wait until today for now.

I was busy today because of is first place.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

examples.text: 그냥 내버려 둬, 쟤 완전 취했어.
examples.trans: Just leave him alone, he is completely wasted.
The topic of that guy/girl came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

examples.text: 저렇게 단순한 애랑 붙으면 케미가 살 수도 있단 말이지.
examples.trans: Pairing up with a simple guy like him could create great chemistry.
Today's atmosphere is truly like that.

examples.text: 제가 섭외했다기보다는 진심이 전달이 된 걸까요?
examples.trans: Rather than me casting her, maybe my sincerity got across?
The topic of delivery, getting across came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: verb deliver

examples.trans: Deliver a message.
Deliver it.

Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금

meanings.en: to like, to be fond of
meanings.note: Takes an object marked with 을/를.

examples.trans: What kind of food do you like?
I like listening to music.
What time is it now?
I'll leave right now.

meanings.note: Used as progressive -고 (지켜보고).

examples.text: 멀리서 지켜보고 계실 부모님, 보고 싶고 또 사랑한다고 전하고 싶고요.
examples.trans: To my parents watching from afar, I want to tell you how much I miss you and love you.
Let us do that (watching over me) right away.

meanings.note: used to emphasize an adjective or adverb

examples.trans: The food is really delicious today.
Time really flies.

meanings.note: Used as honorific + -고 (챙겨주시고).

examples.text: 제가 참 실수 너무 많이 했는데 앞에서 툴툴거리면서도 뒤에서 챙겨주시고 정말 감사했어요, 그리고 1박 2일 라준모 피디님!
examples.trans: Though I made so many mistakes, thank you to Tak Ye-jin for grumbling up front while caring for me behind the scenes—and Producer Ra Joon-mo of 2 Days & 1 Night!
Let us do that (looking out for me and) right away.

examples.text: 나랑 예진이는 초등학교 때부터 그냥 친구야.
examples.trans: Ye-jin and I have simply been friends since elementary school.
The topic of elementary school came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Used as concessive -면서도 (툴툴거리면서도).

examples.text: 제가 참 실수 너무 많이 했는데 앞에서 툴툴거리면서도 뒤에서 챙겨주시고 정말 감사했어요, 그리고 1박 2일 라준모 피디님!
examples.trans: Though I made so many mistakes, thank you to Tak Ye-jin for grumbling up front while caring for me behind the scenes—and Producer Ra Joon-mo of 2 Days & 1 Night!
Let us do that (grumbling while still) right away.

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Determiner form of 하나, used before a noun counter.

examples.trans: one person
one hour

meanings.note: Used as indirect request (해달라고).

examples.text: 신디 1위 발표 후에 소감만 아주 간단하게 해달라고 수신호 좀 해주세요!
examples.trans: Give a hand signal on the floor asking Cindy to keep her acceptance speech super brief after the winner announcement!
Let us do that (asking her to keep) right away.

meanings.note: Compound of 하다 (to do) and 주다 (to give).

examples.trans: Please help me (do helping for me).
Please do this for me.
I ate alone today.
I can do it well by myself too.

meanings.note: Can also function as a noun
Used as noun + time -에 (후에).

examples.text: 피디님은 10년 후에 내가 뭐 하고 있을지 이런 거 다 예상이 되시죠? 나는 안 돼요.
examples.trans: You can easily picture what you will be doing ten years from now, right, Producer? I cannot.

examples.text: 10년 후의 내 모습 난 모르겠어요. 10년 후 아니라 5년 후, 1년 후도 모르겠어요.
examples.trans: I cannot picture myself in ten years—forget ten years, I do not even know five years or one year ahead.
